newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Reserve Bank says has offset Telkom flows.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Reserve Bank says has offset Telkom flows.

text.p: The South Africa Reserve Bank (SARB) said on Thursday it had finished mopping up the roughly $1 billion flow of funds into the financial system resulting from the part-privatisation of Telkom.
"It went fine. As far as we're concerned, everything should work out well," SARB deputy governor James Cross told Reuters.
Cross said the SARB had drained a total of about 4.8 billion rand from the system to offset about $1 billion due to South African telecommunications utility Telkom following its part-privatisation.
The amount had been sold forward to the SARB for delivery from today onward and might have had sharply reduced money market rates if not for the central bank's on-market activities.
"We've done foreign exchage swaps for quite a large part of the money to be invested by Telkom, roughly three billion rand," Cross said.
The swaps involved the central bank selling U.S. dollars -- thereby withdrawing rand from the system -- and buying U.S. dollar forwards with maturities of up to seven days.
Cross added natural month-end tightening of the money market due to note flows would be partially offset by the staggered maturity of the swaps over the balance of the month.
"The note flows reverse next week and we have quite a bit of movement out of the market and we can let our swaps mature if that happens."

He said the SARB had also swapped with the Treasury about one billion rand of zero coupon stock held against the government's accumulated forward exchange losses for a range of interest-bearing securities.
These bonds were then sold into the local debt market along with some light pre-funding debt sales, Cross said.
Cross said the sales were not responsible for a kick up in the benchmark R150 yields over the last few days.
"What we did, we'd done a week or more ago and settled for yesterday and today," he said.
The R150 was last at 15.20 percent after closing Friday around 14.89 percent.

In the absence of unexpectedly large government spending shocks, the SARB's Telkom strategy would keep the money market shortage around current levels, which the bank viewed as appropriate, Cross said.
The Reserve Bank earlier reported South Africa's money market shortage as barely changed on Wednesday having edged down to 6.453 billion from 6.658 billion rand on Tuesday.
Cross said the SARB strategy for future privatisation inflows would depend on monetary policy at the time.
